criminal_incidents.source_title: Delhi court rejects bail plea of Al Falah University chairman in money laundering case - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: NEET paper leak case: Supreme Court directs Centre, NTA to file affidavit - India Today
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **CBI** has secured a five-day remand for the mother-in-law and husband of **Twisha Sharma**, who died after allegedly taking an exam, in connection with the case. The Supreme Court is demanding details from the central government and the National Testing Agency regarding the NEET paper leak, while a parliamentary review meeting is underway to address the crisis.  The Education Minister has acknowledged lapses and promised a secure retest for all candidates.

recent_articles.title: ‘Claims of vishwaguru but...’: Rahul Gandhi, Arvind Kejriwal hit out at PM Modi over CUET-UG exam 2026 delay | Today News
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, **Atishi**, and other Opposition leaders criticized the **Narendra Modi** government's handling of the Common University Entrance Test (CUET-UG) 2026 after technical glitches caused disruptions at several examination centers across India.  The **National Testing Agency (NTA)** confirmed that a technical glitch by its service provider, **Tata Consultancy Services (TCS)** delayed the commencement of the exam on May 30th. The agency revised the afternoon shift schedule and provided full duration to morning-session candidates.

recent_articles.title: CBSE OSM Coempt TCS row | CBSE on screen marking row: Rahul Gandhi says ‘rules’ bent to favour Coempt, cites TCS loss in auction - Telegraph India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi** criticized the **Modi government** over the CBSE exam evaluation controversy, alleging that the board lowered technical requirements to favor **COEMPT Eduteck Private Limited**, a company with a poor track record. He demanded an independent judicial probe into the contract awarding process and accused the government of prioritizing its survival over student well-being.  **Piyush Goyal**, the Union commerce minister, countered Gandhi's claims, accusing him of "propaganda" while **Dharmendra Pradhan**, the Union education minister, defended the board's actions. Other prominent figures like **Priyanka Chaturvedi** and **Mohammed Zubair** have also raised concerns about potential manipulation and a coordinated campaign to promote the OSM system.

recent_articles.title: TMC panchayat member promises to return cut money, villagers blare reminders on loudspeakers - India Today
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Villagers in West Bengal's Cooch Behar district are using loudspeakers to remind a **Trinamool Congress** (TMC) leader, **Jyotsna Barman**, of a promised refund for "cut money" collected from beneficiaries of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana.  The villagers allege that they were forced to pay commissions ranging from Rs 5,000 to Rs 25,000 to secure benefits and avoid delays in future installments during the previous TMC regime. The deadline for returning the "cut money" is June 4th, and residents have threatened fresh protests if the promise is not kept.

recent_articles.title: J-K govt to file review petition in Supreme Court for TET review
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Jammu and Kashmir** government announced it will file a review petition in the Supreme Court regarding the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) issue. Education Minister Sakina Itoo stated that the government has acted responsibly and proactively to protect teacher interests, and the review petition will be filed before the apex court within the coming week. The decision follows the government's previous order to keep the TET designation in abeyance until further orders.

recent_articles.title: Claims of being vishwaguru but can't conduct single exam: Rahul's dig at PM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, leader of the **Congress**, criticized **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** for the delayed CUET-UG 2026 examination, alleging that the government has destroyed the education system.  He accused **Modi** of being unable to conduct even a single examination properly despite claiming to be a "vishwaguru." **Gandhi** stated that this failure is impacting millions of students and will hold **Modi** accountable for his actions.

recent_articles.title: ‘Technical glitch’ delays CUET-UG 2026 exam at some centres - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The National Testing Agency (NTA)** announced a delay of over two hours for the first shift of the Common University Entrance Test-Undergraduate (CUET-UG) on Saturday, May 30, 2026, due to technical glitches at some examination centres. **Tata Consultancy Services (TCS)** was blamed for the delay, which affected candidates across different states. The NTA stated that the issue has been resolved and compensatory time will be provided to all candidates.  The second shift of the exam was also revised with entry starting at 1 p.m. and the examination beginning at 4 p.m.

recent_articles.title: PM’s silence on CBSE OSM controversy shows he cares more about his govt’s survival than students’ future: Rahul Gandhi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, criticized **COEMPT Edutek's** win of the Central Board of Secondary Education’s (CBSE) on-screen marking contract, alleging that tender norms were manipulated to favor the company.  He questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi's silence on the controversy and claimed that the contract was awarded despite technical requirements being relaxed for COEMPT. **Gandhi** also highlighted concerns about the evaluation system's flaws and urged an independent judicial probe into all contracts awarded to **COEMPT**.

recent_articles.title: Indian Air Force likely to oversee transport of NEET-UG re-test papers - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The government** is considering using the **Indian Air Force (IAF)** to manage logistics and transportation for the NEET-UG 2026 re-test, scheduled for June 21.  A high-level meeting was held at the residence of **Defence Minister Rajnath Singh**, attended by **Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan** and **Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia**. The IAF will provide transportation and logistics support to secure question papers from printing presses to examination centers across the country, aiming to minimize leak risks.  The final decision is pending consultations with the Prime Minister's Office.

recent_articles.title: 16 students died in overnight fire at girls' school in Kenya - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Julius Ogamba**, the **Education Minister of Kenya**, confirmed that a fire at the Utumishi Girls School in Gilgil, Kenya, resulted in the deaths of 16 students and injuries to 79 others. The cause of the fire is still under investigation, but school fires are common in Kenyan boarding schools, often attributed to arson or electrical faults.

recent_articles.title: Tamil Nadu’s rights of utmost importance, never said will surrender that: Higher Education Minister - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **P. Viswanathan**, Tamil Nadu Higher Education Minister, defended his statement that the new government would not follow previous policies regarding university governance, particularly concerning the Chief Minister's role as Chancellor. He clarified that he made a general comment and emphasized the state's commitment to protecting its citizens' rights. The **DMK** and other political parties criticized his remarks, accusing him of surrendering state rights.

recent_articles.title: Glitches in CBSE portal leave Class 12 students seeking re-evaluation hassled - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following complaints from students and parents about the new On-Screen Marking (OSM) system, **Union Minister for Education Dharmendra Pradhan** requested a detailed report from the **Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)**. The OSM system, which replaced traditional paper evaluation, faced technical glitches leading to issues with re-evaluation, portal crashes, and blurred answer sheet scans.  Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh criticized the government's handling of the situation, calling for the resignation of **Dharmendra Pradhan**.  The CBSE has extended the deadline for re-evaluation applications and is working to address technical issues with the system.

recent_articles.title: Inclusion of Maithili in CBSE curriculum will connect future generation to their roots: Bihar CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary** hailed the decision by the **Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)** to include Maithili as a subject at the secondary level starting in 2026-27.  The move, supported by **BJP leader Gopal Ji Thakur**, was requested by Mr. Thakur and confirmed by **Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan** and **Minister of State for Education Jayant Chaudhary**. **Sanjay Saraogi**, Bihar BJP President, also welcomed the decision as a tribute to Maithili's cultural heritage and linguistic pride.  Mr. Saraogi emphasized that the inclusion will promote language learning and cultural understanding among future generations.

recent_articles.title: CBSE again extends deadline for scanned answer book requests till May 25 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)** extended the deadline for students to request scanned copies of their evaluated answer books for Class 12 board exams until May 25 midnight. The extension follows complaints from students about difficulties accessing the portal.  **Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan** sought support from the **Union Finance Ministry** to overhaul the CBSE payment gateway system and has directed IIT-Madras and IIT-Kanpur teams to assist in resolving technical issues.

recent_articles.title: Minister’s assurance on Plus One seats brings relief to north Kerala students - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **General Education Minister N. Samsudheen** has announced that the marginal increase of Plus One seats and additional batches allotted last year will be included in the admissions process, offering relief to North Kerala districts facing severe seat shortages. The state cabinet is scheduled to meet on Monday (May 25, 2026) to approve the rollout of the admissions process.  The previous Left Democratic Front government had allocated additional batches and a marginal increase of seats, but these were announced after the allotment process began last year.

recent_articles.title: Janivara and hijab row: KEA to turn down demand by 3 students for re-exam in all subjects - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Three students who were forced to remove their janivara during the Physics Common Entrance Test (CET-2026) in Bengaluru have rejected **KEA’s** offer for a re-examination of just the Physics paper. They instead demanded a re-examination for all four subjects and the best of two scores be considered for ranking.  The **Higher Education Department** has suspended staff at Krupanidhi College, while the parents of the student who refused to remove her hijab have requested help from the **KEA**.

recent_articles.title: Kerala seeks urgent intervention over CBSE Plus Two evaluation complaints - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kerala's** General Education Minister N. Samsudheen has requested the **Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)** and the **Union government** to intervene in the controversy surrounding the evaluation of CBSE Class XII examination papers under the On-Screen Marking (OSM) system.  Samsudheen cited concerns about low marks, unclear answer sheets, and delays in revaluation processes. **Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas** has accused the Central government of failing to address recurring irregularities in centrally-conducted examinations, demanding the resignation of **Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan**.

recent_articles.title: CPI(M) demands scrapping NTA, seeks Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Communist Party of India (Marxist)** demanded the scrapping of the **National Testing Agency (NTA)** over alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak, calling for sweeping changes to the centralized examination system. The party also called for the resignation of Union Education Minister **Dharmendra Pradhan**, alleging repeated failures and loss of credibility by the agency.  The CPI(M) expressed concern over the impact on students' mental health and financial well-being due to the alleged leak, demanding an impartial probe into the matter and strong action against those responsible.

recent_articles.title: I don’t think the ruling party has the stomach for sarcasm, says Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Cockroach Janta Party** (CJP), a youth-led satirical political group, had its website taken down on Saturday, May 23, 2026 at 9 a.m.  Founder Abhijeet Dipke accused the **Indian Government** of orchestrating the takedown, claiming it was due to the CJP's growing popularity and online movement demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan following the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak. The CJP, formed in response to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s controversial “cockroach” remark, rapidly gained traction with over 22 million followers on social media before being blocked by authorities citing national security concerns. Dipke claims his personal accounts were also hacked and he has received death threats.  Despite the takedown, the CJP is not yet a registered political party.

recent_articles.title: Lakshmi could have been a child bride - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lakshmi**, a 16-year-old girl from Uttar Pradesh, wrote a song expressing her desire to continue her education and resist early marriage. Her father initially dismissed the message but was persuaded by **anganwadi workers** and **village pradhan**.  The village now features painted messages advocating for change in response to Lakshmi's powerful lyrics.

recent_articles.title: Congress workers clash with police in Jaipur during stir against NEET-UG paper leak - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** party workers clashed with **police** in **Rajasthan** on Thursday during a protest against the NEET-UG exam paper leak.  Led by **State Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra**, the protesters demanded the resignation of **Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan** and the dissolution of the **National Testing Agency**. The demonstrators, carrying banners and placards, were forcibly dispersed using water cannons. Some protesters suffered minor injuries.

recent_articles.title: NEET paper leak row: Congress demands resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leaders demanded the resignation of **Dharmendra Pradhan**, the **Union Education Minister**, over the NEET-UG paper leak scandal.  They accused the government of a "money-making racket" involving people linked to the ruling establishment and claimed that the incident had caused immense trauma for 22 lakh students. **Rahul Gandhi** called for the Prime Minister's intervention, while **Mallikarjun Kharge**, the Congress president, alleged that the Modi government was undermining student credibility through repeated paper leaks.  **Jairam Ramesh**, a Congress general secretary, criticized the government's lack of action and incompetence in addressing exam reforms.

recent_articles.title: Medical Education Minister demands court-monitored probe into NEET paper leak - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Karnataka Medical Education Minister Sharan Prakash Patil** criticized the ongoing investigation into the NEET question paper leak, calling for a court-monitored probe. He expressed concerns that the **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)**'s current investigation lacked transparency and confidence, suggesting powerful individuals were involved in orchestrating the scandal to manipulate MBBS seat sales.

recent_articles.title: NEET paper leak row: Youth Congress protests in Delhi, chief Uday Bhanu Chib detained - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Indian Youth Congress (IYC)** staged a protest in New Delhi demanding the resignation of **Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan** over alleged NEET-UG question paper leaks.  Protesters, including IYC president Uday Bhanu Chib, were detained by police as they marched towards **Pradhan's** residence. The examination was cancelled on May 3rd and a re-test is scheduled for June 21st. The IYC accused the BJP-led government of creating a corrupt system that favors wealthy students while disadvantaging those from poor backgrounds.

recent_articles.title: NSUI holds protest outside Education Minister’s residence over NEET paper leak - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Members of the National Students’ Union of India (NSUI)** protested outside **Dharmendra Pradhan's** residence in Delhi, demanding his resignation following allegations of a paper leak in the NEET-UG 2026 examination. The protesters accused the Education Minister of failing to protect students and demanded a Supreme Court-monitored investigation into the incident, along with action against those involved. **The National Testing Agency (NTA)** cancelled the exam and announced it would be retaken at a later date.

recent_articles.title: Education Budget will grow every year, says Telangana CM Revanth Reddy - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy** announced that the **Telangana government** will prioritize education, aiming for a 15% allocation in future budgets, gradually increasing from the current 7.6%.  He highlighted the implementation of several initiatives since December 2023, including teacher recruitment, DSC notifications, and global exchange programs. The "Exclusive Education Week" celebrations aim to showcase progress and improve learning facilities across the state. **Mr. Reddy** emphasized that education is an investment in the future and stressed the importance of teachers in building a better society.

recent_articles.title: Why a ministerial vacancy nearly delayed Class 12 Board exam results in T.N. - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The School Education Department of Tamil Nadu** postponed the release date for Class 12 State Board exam results due to a lack of a Minister to authorize the announcement. This decision caused significant disappointment among students, teachers, and parents as it disrupted their preparation plans.  After facing backlash from various stakeholders, including child rights groups and educationists, the department reversed its decision and released the results on May 8th, as scheduled. Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar urged the department to release the scores without delay.

recent_articles.title: NHA recognises innovators for developing AI systems for healthcare claims processing and fraud detection - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The National Health Authority (NHA)** concluded the Auto-Adjudication Hackathon Showcase 2026 at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, recognizing winning teams for AI-driven solutions to improve healthcare claims processing under the **Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY).**  The hackathon, organized by **IndiaAI Mission** and IISc Bengaluru, saw over 3,500 registrations and more than 600 participants. Teams developed AI systems for clinical document classification, radiological image analysis, and forgery detection, with **Team Nirnaya** winning the top prize in the "Clinical Document Classification and Compliance to Standard Treatment Guidelines" category.  Winning teams received cash prizes ranging from ₹2 lakh to ₹5 lakh, and their solutions could be considered for future deployment within the AB PM-JAY ecosystem.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal Cabinet 2026: From Dilip Ghosh to Agnimitra Paul, Ministers who were sworn in along with Suvendu Adhikari - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, newly sworn in as the Chief Minister of West Bengal, inducted five new ministers into his cabinet on Saturday. The swearing-in ceremony was attended by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Union Ministers Amit Shah, Rajnath Singh, J. P. Nadda, and Dharmendra Pradhan**, among other BJP leaders.  **Dilip Ghosh**, a senior BJP leader who secured victory in the Kharagpur seat, **Agnimitra Paul**, a fashion designer-turned-legislator who won Asansol Dakshin, **Ashok Kirtania**, a BJP stalwart who gained victory in Bangaon Uttar, and **Kshudiram Tudu**, a former school teacher from Ranibandh (ST) constituency, were among the newly appointed ministers.  **Nisith Pramanik**, a key face of BJP from North Bengal, was also inducted into the cabinet.

recent_articles.title: NHA, IndiaAI Mission and IISc showcase human-centric AI solutions to transform health claims under AB PM-JAY - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **National Health Authority (NHA)** and its partners, **IndiaAI Mission** and the **Indian Institute of Science (IISc)**, hosted an auto-adjudication hackathon showcasing AI solutions for healthcare claims management under the **Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY)**.  Teams presented AI systems capable of analyzing medical documents, interpreting radiological images, detecting document forgery, and streamlining claim processing. The event highlighted the use of AI/ML to improve the speed, accuracy, transparency, and efficiency of claims adjudication while reducing fraud and manual intervention.

recent_articles.title: NEET-UG 2026 held across 551 cities in India, 14 abroad - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan** visited the **National Testing Agency (NTA)** headquarters on Sunday, May 3, 2026, to assess the readiness for the NEET-UG 2026 examination. The examination was conducted across 551 cities in India and 14 cities abroad, with nearly 23 lakh registered candidates taking the test under strict protocols.  The **NTA** oversaw the logistics, coordination, and monitoring systems for a seamless exam process.

recent_articles.title: Delhi court rejects bail plea of Al Falah University chairman in money laundering case - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Jawad Ahmed Siddiqui**, chairman of the **Al Falah University** group, had his regular bail plea denied by a Delhi court on Saturday.  The **Enforcement Directorate (ED)** opposed the request, citing the seriousness of the money laundering allegations and ongoing investigations. **Siddiqui**, arrested in November 2025 for allegedly generating illicit funds through student fees, remains in judicial custody. A separate ED probe is also underway.

recent_articles.title: Bengaluru road rage: Couple assaulted by bikers after warning against rash riding - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Electronic City police** have registered a case against three motorists for allegedly assaulting a West Bengal couple after a road rage incident in Bettadasanapura, Bengaluru. The incident occurred when the couple confronted a group of youths performing dangerous driving maneuvers on the road.  The suspects chased the couple's car and assaulted both individuals, causing injuries to **Soumyadeep Sen** and **Vyundreela Pradhan**.  A video of the assault has gone viral, raising concerns about road safety.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal election: Hundreds stage protest over ‘threats’ by TMC workers in Falta - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Hundreds** of villagers in Falta, West Bengal staged a protest demanding safety after alleging threats from **TMC workers**. The protesters blocked the road, claiming local panchayat pradhan Israfil threatened them with attacks. **CRPF deputy commandant** visited the area and assured the demonstrators of their security. **Jehangir Khan**, a TMC candidate, dismissed the allegations and claimed the women were staged by the BJP to engineer arrests before the counting.

recent_articles.title: Pact on foreign language learning set to provide global platform to Rajasthan’s youth - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rajasthan**'s government signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with **English and Foreign Languages University, Hyderabad**, to provide foreign language learning opportunities for youth. The MoU aims to enhance communication skills for tourism and local industries, as well as offer global exposure for students.  The initiative was witnessed by Union Education Minister **Dharmendra Pradhan** and Chief Minister **Bhajan Lal Sharma**.

recent_articles.title: KEERA to be established for structural reforms in engineering education: Minister - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Karnataka government** has decided to establish the **Karnataka Engineering Education Reform Authority (KEERA)**, following recommendations from an Expert Committee on Reforms in Technical Education. The committee, led by former director of **IIIT-B**, S. Sadagopan, proposed structural reforms for engineering education.  The government plans to bring separate legislation to establish KEERA and will discuss the matter soon.

recent_articles.title: Bengaluru weather highlights: Orange alert issued for Bengaluru, south Karnataka districts; traffic police release advisory for commuters - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **CM Siddaramaiah** visited injured individuals after a portion of the Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital compound wall collapsed in Shivajinagar, killing seven people.  The **Medical Education Minister Sharanprakash R. Patil** ordered safety audits for government hospital buildings. The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** issued an orange alert for Bengaluru, urging caution from motorists due to heavy rainfall.

recent_articles.title: Uk Social Media Restrictions: ‘Would impose some form of restrictions’: UK minister Olivia Bailey on under-16 social media use - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The UK government has committed to introducing restrictions on social media use for children under 16, but stopped short of a complete ban. **Education minister Olivia Bailey** stated the government would impose "some form of age or functionality restrictions" and that curfews could be considered alongside age limits. The move comes after a prolonged tussle between the House of Lords and the House of Commons over the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill.  The government plans to publish a progress report within three months, with regulations expected within 12 months.

recent_articles.title: Sagar Mitras thank Nellore MP for six-month extension of PMMSY scheme - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nellore MP Vemireddy Prabhakar Reddy** met with members of the A.P. Sagar Mitra Employees Union to discuss the extension of the Pradhan Mantri Madhya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) welfare scheme. **Mr. Reddy** had previously requested an extension from the Union Minister for Fisheries, **Rajiv Ranjan Singh**, and explained that the six-month extension would allow the Sagar Mitras to continue serving as a bridge between the government and fishermen in coastal villages.

recent_articles.title: Samrat Choudhary approves funds for 75 ITI in first Cabinet meeting as Bihar CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary** approved several initiatives during his first Cabinet meeting, including the establishment of 75 state-of-the-art Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) under the **PM SETU** scheme. The Cabinet also sanctioned ₹305 crore for an 11-acre research park at IIT Patna and an additional grant of ₹39 crore for phase 2 of the Incubation Centre at IIT Patna.  The State Cabinet also decided to develop 11 new satellite townships in the state, prohibiting land sales and construction until a Master Plan is prepared.

recent_articles.title: No seats for DMK regulars: Ponmudi, R. Gandhi, Mano Thangaraj, and Kayalvizhi Selvaraj - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **DMK** has announced its list of 164 candidates for the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections, denying seats to former **Higher Education Minister K. Ponmudi**, **Handloom and Textiles Minister R. Gandhi**, **Dairy Development Minister Mano Thangaraj**, and **Human Resources Management Minister Kayalvizhi Selvaraj**.  **Ponmudi's son Gowtham Sigamani** has been chosen to represent Tirukoilur, while **Gandhi's son Vinod** is contesting from Ranipet.

recent_articles.title: Pradhan claims ‘chaos, corruption’ in Trinamool Congress-led West Bengal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Union Minister Dharmendra Pradhan** sharply criticized **West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee**, accusing her government of creating chaos, appeasement, and corruption in the state.  He stated that public trust in governance has eroded, law and order have collapsed, and development has been hindered by the Trinamool Congress's rule. **Pradhan** further claimed that farmers are facing hardship, unemployment is high among youth, and women feel unsafe due to rising crime. He asserted that growing public anger against the ruling party would lead to a decisive mandate for the Bharatiya Janata Party in the upcoming state assembly elections.

recent_articles.title: Develop century-old schools in Karnataka as heritage institutions: KDA to govt. - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Kannada Development Authority (KDA)** has recommended that at least 31 schools in Karnataka, where prominent figures studied, be developed as "Heritage Schools" to preserve their historical significance. The report also suggests establishing museums within these schools and allocating resources for the development of century-old government schools.  It further proposes a separate cell in the Education Department to manage these schools and prioritize their improvement through increased funding and teacher appointments.

recent_articles.title: CBSE announces results for Class 10 board exams; 93.7% students pass - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Female candidates** outperformed their male counterparts in the **Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)** Class 10 board examination results, with a pass percentage of 94.99% compared to 92.69% for boys.  The top performing regions were South India, particularly Thiruvananthapuram and Vijayawada districts, which achieved 99.79% and 99.58% pass rates respectively. The overall pass percentage was 93.70%, a slight improvement from last year. **Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan** commended students for their hard work while emphasizing that the results do not define one's potential.  The CBSE also highlighted the logistical success of this year's examination cycle, involving over 25 lakh candidates across 84 subjects.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka allows 7.5% fee hike for govt. quota engineering seats in private colleges - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Karnataka government** has approved a 7.5% fee increase for government quota seats in private engineering colleges for the academic year 2026-27.  This decision was made after a meeting with **Higher Education Minister M.C. Sudhakar**, who listened to concerns from private college managements regarding increased costs due to the West Asia crisis and rising staff salaries and equipment maintenance expenses. The fee hike will bring the cost of government quota seats in type-1 private colleges to ₹87,935 and type-2 colleges to ₹87,825, while government engineering colleges will remain unaffected.

recent_articles.title: Konthuruthy river restoration: Kochi Corporation hands aid to 80 families - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kochi Corporation** has disbursed ₹14 lakh each to 80 of the 126 families slated for eviction from the Konthuruthy river puramboke, in compliance with a **Kerala High Court** directive. The assistance, part of a rehabilitation package, was transferred directly to the bank accounts of beneficiary families who submitted documents in accordance with government norms.  The Corporation is bearing the lion's share of the ₹17.64 crore package, allocated from its Plan fund and Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana–Urban along with its own resources. The remaining amount will be provided under the government’s LIFE Mission.

recent_articles.title: Root canal treatment included in Ayushman Bharat-Arogya Karnataka scheme - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Karnataka** government has approved the inclusion of root canal treatment (RCT) under its Ayushman Bharat–Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana-Chief Minister’s Arogya Karnataka (AB PMJAY-CM’s ArK) scheme. The decision aims to improve access to dental care and reduce tooth loss, particularly among low-income groups who often opt for extraction due to the high cost of RCT.  The **Suvarna Arogya Suraksha Trust** (SAST), the nodal agency for the scheme, has been directed to adopt Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS) Tier-3 rates for the procedure, with a capped benefit at 50,000 cases or ₹5 crore.

recent_articles.title: Sharan Prakash Patil takes umbrage at remarks by BJP leaders against Mallikarjun Kharge - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Dr. Sharan Prakash Patil**, **Medical Education Minister**, criticized **BJP leaders** for making "irresponsible" and "disrespectful" remarks against **AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge**.  Patil condemned the comments, arguing that they are being blown out of proportion and comparing them to past instances of similar attacks by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** on Congress leaders. He also questioned the basis for comparisons made by **Union Home Minister Amit Shah** against **Jawaharlal Nehru**, emphasizing the Congress's commitment to non-alignment and condemnation of aggression without supporting war.

recent_articles.title: SPMVV Vice-Chancellor unveils book on food analysis - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sri Padmavati Mahila Visvavidyalayam (SPMVV)** Vice-Chancellor V. Uma released a new textbook on food analysis authored by **Institute of Pharmaceutical Technology Professor Galla Rajitha**.  The 250-page book, funded under the Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM-USHA) scheme, aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of food analysis for undergraduate and postgraduate students, researchers, and professionals. The publication is expected to benefit those in the fields of food quality assessment and safety evaluation.

recent_articles.title: T.N. CM Stalin, Union Minister clash over three-language formula ahead of T.N. polls - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)**'s announcement to implement a three-language formula starting in 2026-27 has sparked a heated debate between the **Tamil Nadu** government and the **Union Government**.  **Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin** criticized the policy as an attempt at "Hindi imposition" and argued it undermines Tamil Nadu's linguistic identity, while **Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan** defended the policy as promoting multilingualism and dismissing concerns about reciprocity. The debate highlights the tension between federalism and language policies in India.

recent_articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly polls: Sundapur villagers withdraw poll boycott after assurance on road project in Erode district - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Residents** of Sundapur in the Bargur Hills, under the Anthiyur Assembly constituency, withdrew a boycott threat against the April 23 election after officials assured them their demand for a road would be addressed. The hamlet, with limited access due to a lack of a motorable road, had been facing difficulties accessing healthcare and transportation services.  **Officials** from the Anthiyur constituency visited the village multiple times but failed to resolve the issue until an assurance was given that the road project would be completed after the election.

recent_articles.title: T.N. Assembly election: Stalin challenges Prime Minister Modi to repeat Bihar poll jibe during T.N. campaign - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **M.K. Stalin**, the DMK president and Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, challenged **Narendra Modi**, the Prime Minister, to repeat his accusation about workers' treatment in Tamil Nadu during his upcoming roadshow in Chennai.  Stalin criticized the Prime Minister's claims about Tamil Nadu being a haven of peace and accused him of harboring hatred for the state. He also addressed concerns over denied Metro Rail projects for Coimbatore and Madurai, highlighting the DMK's achievements and seeking votes based on development and welfare measures.

recent_articles.title: KSRTC’s training programmes earn World HRD Congress Award - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC)** received the **World HRD Congress Award 2026** for its comprehensive training programs. The award recognizes KSRTC's extensive initiatives, including fuel efficiency training, road safety awareness, and simulator-based training, across five training centers.  The organization also provides free driving licenses to Scheduled Caste candidates under the PM-AJAY scheme and collaborates with the Directorate of Minorities for similar initiatives for minority communities. The award was received by **Latha T.S.** and **A.S. Geethanjali**.

recent_articles.title: BJP puts up united front as Suvendu Adhikari files nomination for Nandigram - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, former BJP state president, filed his nomination for the upcoming West Bengal Assembly elections on March 30th. He is contesting from Nandigram and Bhawanipur, challenging incumbent Chief Minister **Mamata Banerjee**.  He was accompanied by **Dilip Ghosh**, former BJP state president, and Union minister **Dharmendra Pradhan**. The BJP has accused **Mamata Banerjee** of threatening voters and violating the Model Code of Conduct. A delegation of senior BJP leaders met with the Election Commission to complain about her actions.

recent_articles.title: ‘A double-engine govt. will de-risk people from political conflicts that hurt their development’: Rajeev Chandrasekhar - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rajeev Chandrasekhar**, the Bharatiya Janata Party's State president in Kerala, is leading the party's efforts to challenge the LDF-UDF duopoly. He faces a tough battle in Nemom, where he competes against incumbent MLA V. Sivankutty and former Congress MLA K.S. Sabarinadhan.  While the BJP saw gains in local body elections, its vote share remains lower than in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. Chandrasekhar emphasizes his party's outreach to minority communities and addresses concerns about incidents of violence against religious minorities. He argues that the BJP is not solely responsible for such events but acknowledges the need for law enforcement.  He also highlights the contrasting perspectives on disaster relief funds, with the LDF criticizing the Centre while pointing to the BJP-led government's own achievements in areas like health and education.

recent_articles.title: T.N. Assembly election: DMK candidate list includes 60 fresh faces and 4 Mayors - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **DMK** released its list of candidates for the upcoming Assembly elections, retaining many Ministers and introducing 60 new faces. The list includes four Mayors, 19 women candidates, and nominees with diverse professional backgrounds, including doctors, engineers, advocates, and PhD holders.  Senior Minister Duraimurugan will contest from Katpadi constituency, while R. Mahesh, N. Dinesh Kumar, Shan Ramanathan, and S. A. Sathya are among the Mayors entering the fray. Ministers dropped include R. Gandhi, Mano Thangaraj, and Kayalvizhi Selvaraj, with former Minister K. Ramachandran opting out due to health reasons.

recent_articles.title: Former AIADMK leaders allotted DMK tickets - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK)** has awarded tickets to several former members of the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) and their supporters for upcoming elections. **O. Panneerselvam**, a former Chief Minister, will contest from Bodinayakanur Assembly constituency while **R. Vaithilingam** will run in Orathanadu.  **Manoj Pandian** has been chosen to represent Alangulam, having defeated a DMK candidate in the 2021 election. **P. Palaniappan**, a former AIADMK leader, has also received a ticket for Pappireddipatti.  **Thoppu N.D. Venkatachalam** will contest from Perundurai after joining the DMK in 2021.
